post.title: What a dividend is, explained with acorns
post.ig:
100 shares can pay you $200 a year. Here's the catch.
A dividend is a slice of profit paid to shareholders, often every quarter.
Example: 100 shares x $0.50 a quarter = $200 a year. At $50 a share, that's a 4% yield.
The S&P 500 yielded about 1% in Sept 2026, and on the ex-dividend date a stock usually drops by about the dividend.
Sources: SEC Investor.gov, S&P Dow Jones Indices.
